Higher demand Population increase -> higher demand for freshwater resources globally for domestic and economic activities Higher living standards Water footprint = the level of development More money -> more meat and diary products -> more water comsumption -> larger water footprints Decreasing supply Water pollution Toxic or dirty substance e.g. industrial waste or sewage enters lakes, rivers and groundwater4 -> Cannot be used Climate change Some region recieve less precipitation -> lower freshwater supply 2 How is it in China ¶ Water problems in China Water Scarcity China has a lot of freshwater But not much per capita -> water may not meet people's needs bc imbalance between water supply and demand Regional and sesonal differences North: less water South: more water Winter: less water Flooding and drought Related to the distribution of precipitation Location of freshwater resources Most freshwater resources are obtained from rivers and lakes River basin = Area that precipitation flows into river aka drained by a river Most important: Chang Jiang, Zhu Jiang, Heilong Jiang (From most to least) Wet and Dry regions 32% of land is humid Mainly found in the southern region 53% of land is Semi-arid or arid Mainly found in the nothern and north-western regions South wet, North-western dry Factors of Percipitation Large part of China has monsoon climates Monsoons = winds that change direction seasonally blowing opposite way in summer and winter Summer Land absorb heat quickily -> air becomes hot and rise -> **air pressure low ** Water absorb heat slower than land -> air cooler and sink -> air pressure higher Air moves from high-pressure area to low pressure-area -> blow from sea towards land (southern and eastern part of Asia) Which are onshore winds and summer monsoons carry much moisture -> wet summer Winter Opposite: release heat faster for land / slower for sea Distance from the sea Onshore wind carry moisture Reach inland areas -> moisture lost Eastern coast recieve more percipitation than the inland regions Relation of percipitation to freshwater resources and water problems Precipitation recieved in a place varies with seasons Area affected by monsoon recieve higher rainfall in summer then in winter Distribution is highly uneven Wet season: higher volume of river flow More water in wet season(summer) water scarcity is more severe in winter Dry season longer then normal -> drought rainfall in the wet season is exceptionally high -> flooding 3 Worsening of water scarcity ¶ bc Increasing demand, Decreasing supply 3.1 Why is demand increasing? ¶ Increase in population Continuous population growth -> larger demand for water Economic development Since open policy rapid economic growth Economic activities demand for huge amount of water (e.g. manufacturing, agricultural activities) Water is also use ineffectively Only 1/3 of irrigation water is used effectively freshwater resource used to produce one unit of product is way more then more developed countries Rise in living standards Rapid economic development -> income increase -> living standard improve Demand for more food and consumer goods -> more water is needed for different uses Low cost of water Cost of water is low Not enough economic incentive for water users to save water Many people are not aware of the importance of water conservation -> waste water 3.2 Water supply decrease ¶ Water pollution Rapid population growth + economic development -> higher use of water resoruces -> increase in the discharge in sewage (doubled from 1980 to 2015) If sewage is discharged into lakes and rivers w/o treatment -> water pollution Some farmers apply too much chemical (pesticides, fertilizers) Excess chemicals + untreated animal waste may be washed into rivers and lakes by rainfall -> cause water pollution + pollute groundwater Depletion of Groundwater Water stored underground From water that seep into the ground Major source of freshwater supply if lakes and river are not enough -> dig wells Nothern China freshwater resources are not enough to meet the demand for water People rely on groundwater natural groundwater recharge is small Overdrawing groundwater will reduce groundwater storage -> further decrease freshwater supply Avalibility is a security issue -> must have a secure water supply 4 Problem of drought ¶ 4.1 What is it ¶ Rainfall in an area is much lower then normal for a long period of time A natural hazard (if a area is always dry its arid ) 4.2 Impacts of drought in China ¶ On people Farming Lack of water for irrigation / pastures -> Crop faliure, livestock die, farm production drops -> food shortages Industry : Lack of water for processing + cooling: Industrial production will decline Power generation : Water level drop -> hydroelectric power (HEP) production drop Transport: Water transport will be disrupted Daily domestic use Not enough water to use May need to carry out water rationing(restrict water supply) Will cause inconvenience and affect people's health On environment Lakes and rivers dry up -> Cut-off of river X vegatiation -> topsoil blown away -> **soil erosion ** -> intensify desertification (makes land unproductive) -> Sandstorm will be more common plants and animals die -> ecosystem adversely affected 4.3 Where does drought usually occur ¶ X western part Mainly found in the nothern and southern part of China 4.4 Causes of drought ¶ Physical factors (environmental) Variation in rainfall Drought is related to rainfall variability Large part of china is affected by monsoon Timing and strength vary between years Wet summer monsoon come late / dry winter monsoon come early Weak summer monsoon: carry less moisture High temperature Higher temperature -> higher evaporation rates Human factors Human induced climate change human activilies emit Green House Gases into the atmosphere -> climate change -> rainfall in China decreasing High water consumption Water cannot meet the demand even in normal years -> Overdrawing of groundwater Water recieved is below normal -> water avalible is even less -> Drought intensified Reduced water supply Water wastage and water pollution -> decrease in freshwater supply -> intensifies drought 5 Ways of tackling water scarcity ¶ 5.1 China's effort ¶ Increasing supply Building dams and resivoris Wet season: reservoirs behind the dams can docs.text: [[Renaissance]] [[Scientific revolution]] - A intellectual and cultural movement between the mid-17th and 18th centuries - Stated that people enjoyed ==natural rights== (equality, liberty) - opposed political and social inequalities Causes - Change of value: Promoted idea of humanism -> applied to social and political aspects - ==Discontent with absolutism== - Absolute rulers promoted the '== divine rights of kings ==' - -> Europeans began to criticize absolutism Ideas - == Laws of nature == - Enjoyed inborn rights of equality and liberty - States and government were set up to protect - == Social contract == - About people and government - ==Locke== + ==Rousseau== suggested - power of government came from people - if government breaks contract and cannot protect people natural rights - people have the right to overthrow - ==Separation of powers== - Montesquieu suggested - ==legislature== , ==executive== and ==judiciary== - prevent absolute rule - ==Constitution + Reforms== - Voltaire suggested - Limit the power of kings and protect people's rights (freedom of speech, press, religion) Spread - academic journals became popular and was a important mean for Europeans to absorb Enlightenment ideas - Publishers were eager to translate and print -> idea became ==widespread== Impact - ==Liberating== minds of European: Awakened Europeans to political system and pursuit to liberty - == Spread == in Europe and Americans -> American Revolution + French Revolution - Enlightenment ideas -> Absolute rulers gave more rights ( Enlightened despots )

peasants left manors and lived in towns - -> freeman -> greater freedom and time for art and learning - -> Renaissance Spread of eastern knowledge - Arab know more than European - Crusades (11-13 centries) encouraged knowledge exchange between Europe and Arab world - prohibited dissecion of the 'scared' human body - During renassance - scholars studied the original copies - found difference form church translation - Verified theories with observation and research - known as ' scientific enquiry ' - Discoveries in Medicine - Fracastoro : diseases ware spread by bacteria (bread on decayed matter) - Vesalius : Dissected human bodies, described human skeleton, organs and muscles in his book - Renaissance: revived the ancient Greco-Roman civilization - made great achievement and developed rapidly - laid the Foundation for moderm European civilization Rise of humanistic education - Aim of education is not clergy(e.g. pope) but ' renassance man ' - people went to non church school to get worldly knowledge - -> develop European education and culture Intellectual liberation ( the process of freeing the mind ) - Renassance freed teh minds of Europeans - NO longer obeyed traditional authority blindly - valued rational thinking - led to Reformation , voyages of discovery, the scientific revolution and the elightenment - milestones in the rise of modern europe, starting in Renassance

docs.text: Factors for the First World War ¶ Conflicts among European powers Extreme nationalism Expand aggressively -> Enhance status and influence at any cost Intensified disputes e.g. Germany ('Pan-Germanism') <-> France (Recapture Alsace-Lorraine, Avenge defeat in Franco-Prussian War) Austria-Hungary (Suppress national independence, expand territory) <-> Russia and Serbia ('Pan-Slavism', establish 'Greater Serbia' in Balkan Penisula) Alliance system Triple Alliance (Central powers) Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy (1882) To isolate France Triple Entente (Allied powers) France, Britain, Russia (1907) -> Divided into two rival camps, Turn into large-scale wars with chain reaction of Allies' intervention Scrambling for colonies -> Conflicts Incident Power Description Tunisian Incident France, Italy French occupied Tunisia, Italy protested Fashoda Incident Britain, France In Sudan, divided their sphere of influence Moroccan Crises ... ... Armaments racer Strong military force could safeguard national security and interests Introduced conscription to expand armies -> Increased military expenditures Developed new weapons of mass destruction (e.g. machine guns) Built " Dreadnoughts " (large warships) mainly Britain and Germany -> Reluctant to make concessions in case of conflicts Pre-war Crises First Moroccan Crisis (1905-1906) Kaiser William II visited Morocco and declared its sovereign independence -> Discontent with France Forced to make a concession: Recognise French privileges in Morocco at last Second Moroccan Crisis (1911) France sent troops to Morocco to put down riots Germany sent gunboats to Agadir -> Morocco became a French protectorate -> Relation between Germany and France worsened Bosnian Crisis (1908) Ottoman Empire was in decline -> Austria-Hungary annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina Serbia and Russia wanted to expand -> Finally gave in bc Austria-Hungary was supported by Germany Serbs form a anti-Austrian organisation -> assassination in Sarajevo Two Balkan Wars Ottoman Empire lost a large part of European territory Austria-Hungary wanted to stop Serbia from expanding -> Supported Albania's independence -> Prevented Serbia from gaining access to the sea -> Straining relationship First Balkan War Balkan League (Serbia, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Greece) VS Ottoman Empire Balkan states seized the European territories of the Ottoman Empire Second Balkan War Balkan League - Bulgaria, Ottoman Empire, Romania VS Bulgaria Bulgaria was dissatisfied with the distribution of land after the war -> Bulgaria was defeated Outbreak of the First World War ¶ The Sarajevo incident (1914) Archduke Franz Ferdinand (heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary) were assassinated during a visit to Sarajevo Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia (23 July) Prohibit all anti-Austrian organisations Remove all officials not accepted by the Austro-Hungarian EMpire Allow Austro-Hungarian officials to enter Serbia to suppress anti-Austro-Hungarian activities to investigate the assassination -> Serbia refused to accept -> Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia (28 July) Course and outcome ¶ Turned into a world war under the alliance system Between Central Powers (Triple alliance) and Allied powers (Triple entente) Eastern front: from Baltic Sea to south-eastern Europe Western front: from the North Sea to Switzerland Lasted four years and Allied powers won Central powers 1914: Austria-Hungary, Germany, Ottoman Empire 1915: Bulgaria Allied powers 1914: Serbia, Russia, France 1915: Italy 1916: Portugal, Romania 1917: US, China, ... Paris peace conference ¶ Objectives Re-establish international Order Maintain lasting peace The Big Three Georges Clemenceau (French Prime Minister) Witnessed two invasions of France by Germany -> Hated Germany Called "the Tiger" Germany should be severely punished so it could no longer threaten France David Lloyd George (Britain Prime Minister) Weaken Germany -> No longer threaten British supremacy Sought a balance -> Affect British trade and allow France to become too powerful Woodrow Wilson (American President) Fourteen Points National self-determination Establish a international organisation for keeping peace Advocated a moderate peace settlement Treaty of Versailles Punishing Germany severely Surrender all colonies Cede >10% territory Pay reparations of 6.6 Billions Accept all war guilt Army Greatly reduced in size and almost completely disarmed Establishing and international organisation to keep peace Rearranging European territories according to the principle of national self-determination Impacts Arousing Resentments Germany Defeated countries could not participate in peace conference -> Germans felt treaty was forced upon them Resented Germany needed to accept all war guilt -> strong feeling of revenge Italy: was victorious but didn't get the land promised by Britain and France -> Fascist regimes to lead their countries out of difficult situations League of Nations Geneva, Switzerland Resolve international disputes and promote world peace US refused to join, Germany and Soviet Russia excluded -> limited effectiveness Changing map of Europe Led to the collapse of the four traditional empires (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Russia, Ottoman Empire) New states were founded on the principle of national self-determination e.g. Poland, Hungary,
